map.projection: simple cylindrical, planetocentric latitude, as seen from outside (east to the right)

source.name: NASA Photojournal PIA07782 — Cassini's Best Maps of Jupiter (cylindrical map)

map.processing: Resized to 2048×1024. The Great Red Spot was located automatically (reddest patch 15–30° S) at map x = 36.7% to align the map's longitudes with the spot's current estimated position.
notes: Cassini narrow-angle images from 11–12 December 2000. Jupiter's clouds change constantly: belts, ovals and the Great Red Spot (which has shrunk since) look different today.
